intro: Searching for car insurance near you usually means you want to sort out cover for a car you drive, or are about to drive, and you'd rather talk it through with someone local than work through it alone. Insurance brokers near you can compare options and explain what each policy actually covers. Tell us what you need and we'll introduce you to a suitable UK insurance broker who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for car insurance near them usually need
need_lead: Most people who search this way have a practical reason to get cover sorted, and a local broker can help them make sense of the choices.
needs: You have just bought a car and need cover in place before you can drive it away.
Your renewal quote has come through and you want to see whether a broker can find you something more suitable.
You have changed jobs, moved house or started parking on the street, and your circumstances no longer match your current policy.
You drive a modified car and need a broker who understands how declarations affect cover.
You are adding a young or named driver to a policy and want to make sure the details are recorded accurately.
context_heading: Why it pays to be precise about your details
context: Car insurance is a legal requirement in the UK, and cover generally comes as third party, third party fire and theft, or comprehensive. The premium you are offered depends heavily on details like your annual mileage, where the car is parked overnight, and who else drives it. Small inaccuracies can affect a claim, so it is worth having everything to hand before you speak to a broker.

Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the make, model and year of the car you want to insure, and whether it is new to you.
Let us know whether you need third party, third party fire and theft, or comprehensive cover.
Describe where the car is kept overnight, such as a driveway, garage or on-street parking.
Give an idea of your annual mileage and what the car is mainly used for, such as commuting or social driving.
List any modifications to the car, including factory-fitted options that differ from the standard model.
Mention any named drivers you want on the policy and whether they have their own no-claims discount.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the broker you speak to
questions: Which insurers or schemes will you be approaching for my car insurance quote?
How will you be paid for arranging my policy, and is that included in the quote?
What excesses apply to the policy you are recommending, and how do they affect a claim?
Are there exclusions in this cover that would matter for how I actually use the car?
How will my named drivers' details and any modifications be recorded on the policy?
What should I do if I need to make a change to the policy partway through the year?

faqs.q: Do I legally need car insurance to drive in the UK?
faqs.a: Yes, car insurance is a legal requirement in the UK. Cover is available as third party, third party fire and theft, or comprehensive, and a broker can explain what each level includes.

faqs.q: Will a broker near me be able to find a cheaper quote than my renewal?
faqs.a: It depends on your circumstances, and no one can promise a lower price. A broker can approach insurers on your behalf and explain the differences between quotes, so you can judge what suits you rather than simply picking the lowest figure.

faqs.q: Does my annual mileage really affect my premium?
faqs.a: Yes, mileage is one of the details insurers use when working out a premium, along with where the car is parked. Giving an accurate figure helps make sure your policy matches how you actually use the car.

faqs.q: What happens if I forget to declare a modification?
faqs.a: Modifications must be declared, and failing to do so can affect your cover if you need to claim. Tell your broker about anything that differs from the standard model, including factory-fitted options, so it can be recorded properly.
